full_judgment: 15. Mr. S.B. Barua, the learned Advocate appearing for the state, submits that the accused petitioner exceeded his authority as Accounts Officer of the Upazila as without prior sanction ' or approval from the Education Officer. He sent the bills for payment against the G.P. Fund to the deposited. The contention of Mr. Barua does not Let support from the allegations made in the F.I.R. There is also no document or paper to show that the Accounts Officer passed the hills without having any authority from the Upazila Education Officer. On the prayer of the learned Advocate for the State, the hearing of the case was twice adjourned so as to enable him to bring the documents and papers, if any, seized by the 1.0. but the learned Advocate for the State expressed his inability to produce any such document or paper as he did not receive any response from the Deputy Commissioner, Gaillandlia inspire of his best effort. In the absence of any paper and document we arc to depend entirely on the F.I.R., the charge-sheet and the affidavits. In this case no counter affidavit has been sworn on behalf of the State and the averments made in the application have thus remained unchallenged. Next point raised by Mr. Nurullah is 'the point of limitation. The learned Advocate also submits that the proceeding cannot be allowed to continue beyond the period of limitation without complying the provision of Sections 167(5)(6)(7) Cr. P.C., and hence it is liable to be stopped and the accused petitioner is entitled to be released. We are not inclined to take up the ' point relating to limitation at this stage in this case as we think that the most pertinent question is whether the statement made in the F.I.R. and the charge sheet disclose any prima facie case of Criminal Misappropriation or Criminal Breach of Trust and for that matter initiation and continuation of the case under Section 409 will amount to abuse of the process of Court. As we have already found that there was no allegation of entrustment to and or misappropriation by the accused petitioner of any money said to have been given to and taken by the deposited from their respective G.P. Fund Accounts, we arc of the view that to allow the criminal case to Continue Will amount to causing harassment to the accused petitioner, particularly in the case which was started in the year 1985 and has still been continuing even after the recovery on repayment of loan by the loaners towards the adjustment of Q.P. Fund account which fact has not been controverted by anybody from the side of the prosecution.
